description: Reviewed exceptions to the cmux-remote lane rules (p05-ipc task 152; build-support/remote_lanes.rs states the rules). cmux-ipc build.rs routes every framed command and event of spec/sdk-schema.json by rule, then applies these. A key is a command or event name, a `prefix-*` pattern, or (under `families`) a schema family. `when` refines the lane on one line envelope field (op, mode or scope) the schema declares; a frame never parses its payload, so it rides input when either lane is input and the base lane otherwise. `events.unlisted` routes events a daemon emits that the schema does not declare yet; each leaves the list when the schema declares it. The build refuses an entry that names nothing, repeats its rule's lane or refines on an undeclared field.

loopback.reason: loopback-forward-v1: open, data, credit, shutdown and close of one stream stay ordered, and forwarded bytes never queue ahead of PTY input.

agent-sessions.reason: agent-session-attach-v1: the attach reply, the replay pages and the live records of one attachment stay in one ordered lane, so a record never overtakes the reply it follows.

agent-transfer-*.reason: agent-transfer-v1: bundle pages of up to 4 MiB never queue ahead of PTY input, and the steps of one transfer stay ordered.

read-screen.reason: The reply carries a whole screen; on bulk it never holds control replies behind it.

vt-state.reason: The reply carries the terminal's whole VT state; on bulk it never holds control replies behind it.

paste-image.reason: Image chunks are acknowledged before commit, so they take bulk backpressure; the commit rides input, so the paste keeps its place among keystrokes.

copy.reason: Copying the scrollback returns all of it; the other modes are ordinary mutations.

identify.reason: A read-only lookup never waits behind PTY input or a slow mutation commit; a stalled input lane must not make a live terminal look missing to the client resolving it.

loopback-events.reason: Forwarded loopback bytes and their stream lifecycle stay in one ordered lane, away from keystrokes and control replies.

overflow.reason: An attach overflow (scope surface) ends its stream after the stream's output; a subscription overflow rides control.

scroll-changed.reason: Attach streams send it in order with the output that scrolled. The line has no field that tells a subscription's copy from an attach stream's, so the subscription's copy rides bulk too, as before task 152: it is the one subscription event off control.

agent-inventory-changed.reason: agent-inventory-watch sends it and agent-inventory-watch-ended to one connection; on control a watch-ended never passes a change enqueued before it.

agent-session-record.reason: agent-session-attach-v1 stream (core:server/agent_session_stream.rs): follows the attach reply in one ordered lane.

agent-session-permission.reason: agent-session-attach-v1 stream (core:server/agent_session_stream.rs): follows the attach reply in one ordered lane.

agent-session-closed.reason: agent-session-attach-v1 stream (core:server/agent_session_attach.rs): ends the attachment after its records.
